Energy transition

Chernobyl: Recovery

In March 1986, all four Chernobyl reactors are producing electricity. A month from now, all four will be offline. Part of your job is paying for the cleanup.

Play Chernobyl: Recovery↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR
Starts in
1986
Your term
5 years

Your starting point

You run a model of the regional grid, with coal and oil plants alongside the reactors. After the April disaster, Units 1 and 2 return that fall. Unit 3 stays offline until December 1987. Unit 4 never returns.

Your term runs through February 1991. Blackouts cost you points and you can keep working to restore service afterward. Bankruptcy ends the run.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Restore service between restarts

    Compare what the coal and oil plants can supply now with what new construction could deliver before the surviving reactors return.

  2. 02

    Pay for cleanup

    Unit 4 carries a monthly cleanup bill. You can't sell the reactor, so keep that expense in your budget even after the other units restart.

  3. 03

    Track what customers experience

    At the end of five years, review the service you restored, what customers paid and the emissions your grid produced.

How much service can you restore with the resources you have?
